title: How to build a $10K/month one-person business as a beginner: simple, niche, productized
summary: Iman Gadzhi lays out a stripped-down path to a solo $10K/month business: pick a simple business model, niche down hard, productize with digital products, use AI as leverage, build an audience organically, ship imperfect work, and don't scale before product-market fit.

principles.text: Start with a simple, validated business model; prefer productized digital products over custom service work.
principles.quote: building something once and having the ability to sell it forever.

principles.text: Niche down to a hyper-specific audience and promise; specificity beats a bigger addressable market.
principles.quote: Don't be a fitness coach, please. Instead, be the guy who helps busy dads in their 30s lose their beer belly in 90 days without giving up weekend beers.

principles.text: At $10K/month, run one funnel, one core offer, one clear outcome; double down on what works before expanding.
principles.quote: One funnel, one core offer, and one clear outcome. You find one thing that works, and you double down on it until it's generating consistent revenue.

principles.text: Monetize problems people need solved, not your passion; the market pays for what it needs to learn.
principles.quote: The market does not pay for what you want to teach. It pays for what it needs to learn.

principles.text: Build an organic audience on one platform first; ads can't fix a broken offer or build an audience from scratch.
principles.quote: trying to use ads to fix a broken offer or to build an audience from scratch is just an expensive mistake.

principles.text: Don't scale or hire before product-market fit; perfect the offer, systems, and unit economics first.
principles.quote: Scaling a broken business will just break it faster and cost you more money.
